An ultra-realistic handheld travel vlog filmed by a friend following the main character throughout the day in Bandung, Indonesia. Use the woman from the reference image as the main subject. Portray her as an Indonesian woman naturally exploring Bandung. Maintain her exact facial identity, hairstyle, facial features, skin tone, and body proportions consistently throughout the entire video.

The camera should feel like a genuine personal vlog camera rather than a commercial production. Use natural handheld movement, casual framing, subtle imperfections in human camera operation, and an authentic everyday Indonesian atmosphere. Avoid scripted acting. The woman behaves naturally, interacting with her surroundings as she would in a real travel vlog.

**Morning departure — Bandung neighborhood**

The woman leaves a cozy modern apartment or guesthouse in Bandung carrying a small backpack. She checks her phone, smiles toward the camera, adjusts her hair, and begins walking outside. The camera follows her from behind with slight natural shakiness, as if a close friend is casually filming her.

The morning atmosphere should immediately feel like Bandung: cool fresh air, cloudy-bright morning light, green trees, quiet residential streets, motorcycles passing occasionally, local residents starting their day, and authentic Indonesian architecture. Avoid tropical beach scenery.

**Exploring Bandung**

The camera follows her through the streets of Bandung. She visits a cozy local café with a modern Bandung aesthetic, orders an iced coffee or local drink, briefly talks to the camera, and laughs naturally.

She then continues walking through a lively Bandung neighborhood, passing small local shops, street food vendors, motorcycles, pedestrians, and vintage-style buildings. Include recognizable Bandung atmosphere inspired by areas such as Braga and Dago without making the scene feel like a tourist advertisement.

She casually takes photos with her phone while looking around. The camera remains close to her, capturing spontaneous everyday moments.

**Golden-hour ending**

Golden-hour light begins to appear over the Bandung hills.

She sits at an outdoor viewpoint overlooking the city, holding a drink while quietly watching the sunset. The atmosphere becomes calm and intimate.

The camera slowly moves backward, gradually revealing her, the café terrace, surrounding trees, the Bandung skyline, distant hills, and the warm evening atmosphere.

The final moment should feel like a genuine personal travel memory captured spontaneously by a close friend.

**Visual style:**

Ultra-realistic authentic Indonesian travel-vlog footage. Ultra-realistic smartphone or mirrorless-camera appearance. Natural Bandung daylight and believable environmental lighting. Cool morning atmosphere transitioning into warm golden-hour light.

Casual handheld movement with subtle camera shake and imperfect human operation. Genuine human reactions and spontaneous interactions. Documentary-level realism with highly detailed skin, hair, clothing, Indonesian streets, café interiors, vegetation, motorcycles, buildings, food, and natural environmental textures.

Authentic Bandung atmosphere. Modern Indonesian lifestyle. Natural Indonesian fashion. Realistic local people and everyday activity.

No cinematic commercial aesthetic. No dramatic posing. No artificial transitions. No text overlays. No logos. No face changes. No identity changes. No exaggerated beauty filters. No unrealistic skin smoothing.

The entire 30-second generation should feel like one continuous, coherent day in Bandung captured by a real friend — not a collection of disconnected AI-generated scenes.

Maintain the exact same woman, facial identity, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, and visual appearance throughout the entire video.

20 AI TOOLS YOU SHOULD KNOW IN 2026 🧠

You don’t need to know every AI tool.

Just know the ones that can actually save you time.

Everyone knows ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

I've also included some underrated ones.

1. ChatGPT: Research, writing, coding, analysis and everyday work.

2. Claude: Strong for writing, reasoning, coding and handling long documents.

3. Perplexity: Research and web search when you want answers with sources.

4. Gemini: Useful for research and working across Google’s ecosystem.

5. NotebookLM: Turn your own PDFs, documents and research into an interactive knowledge base.

6. Grok: Useful for real-time conversations, trends and information on X.

7. Cursor: AI-powered coding environment for building and editing software faster.

8. Lovable: Create functional web apps from natural-language instructions.

9. Replit: Build, test and deploy applications with AI assistance.

10. Midjourney: Generate high-quality visuals and creative concepts.

11. Krea: Real-time image generation, enhancement and creative workflows.

12. Ideogram: Particularly good for designs that require accurate text inside images.

13. Runway: AI video generation and editing for creators and teams.

14. Kling AI: Generate realistic AI videos from text and images.

15. ElevenLabs: AI voice generation, dubbing and audio creation.

16. Gamma: Create presentations, documents and visual content quickly.

17. Napkin AI: Turn written ideas into diagrams and visual explanations.

18. Granola: AI meeting notes designed around your actual meetings.

19. Genspark: AI agents that can handle research and multi-step tasks.

20. n8n: Build powerful AI automations by connecting models, APIs and different tools.

You don’t need all 20.

Start with the tools that solve problems you already have.

Learn the workflow, not just the tool.

Bookmark this list. It’ll be useful as you explore more into AI

If I were starting remote work today, here's exactly what I would do:

1️⃣ Choose ONE skill.
Don't try to learn everything at once. Start with Virtual Assistance, Customer Support, Data Entry, Social Media Management, Graphic Design, Writing, or another skill that matches your strengths.

2️⃣ Learn the skill.
Use free resources, YouTube, courses, and practical tutorials. Don't just watch—practice.

3️⃣ Build proof of your skills.
Create 2–3 sample projects, even if you don't have a client yet. Your portfolio should show people what you can actually do.

4️⃣ Set up your professional presence.
Create or optimize your LinkedIn profile and profiles on relevant freelance platforms. Use a clear photo, strong headline, good bio, and showcase your skills.

5️⃣ Start networking.
Connect with people in your industry. Comment thoughtfully on posts. Join communities. Tell people what you do.

6️⃣ Start applying.
Don't wait until you feel 100% ready. Apply for suitable opportunities and tailor your proposal/application to each client.

7️⃣ Keep improving while you earn.
Your first client isn't the finish line. Use every project to gain experience, testimonials, confidence, and better skills.

8️⃣ Be consistent.
Remote work isn't overnight success. You may get ignored, rejected, or hear nothing at first.

Keep going.

If I were starting again, I'd focus less on “How quickly can I make money?” and more on “How valuable can I become?”

Because when your skills become valuable, opportunities become easier to find. 🚀

If you were starting remote work today, what skill would you choose first? Drop it in the comments. 👇

Update on our robot learning project with @aboraatakan at @uwwatai.

We went from ~30% to 99.8% success on our pick-and-place task by updating our policy from a DINO ViT + transformer policy to a CNN + MLP. Our old model was memorizing the training data and transferring poorly to closed-loop rollouts, so we went the other way and made the model smaller.

The attached video is the CNN + MLP policy running in sim on our async inference stack. We demoed it live for a few hours: 4 failures over 2000+ randomized scenes. This experience has been useful to confirm our stack's correctness. We are now ready to move to hardware!

Next: real hardware, diffusion policy, open-weight fine-tunes, and RL.

Reach out if you're interested in collaborating, and stay tuned.
